@graph.description: Jemeluk, Lipah, Bunutan and Gili Selang: a guide to Amed's dive sites, conditions and seasons, plus how to add West Sumbawa to your Bali dive trip.

mainEntity.name: What makes Amed’s diving ecosystem unique compared to other Bali dive destinations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Amed’s diving is special because of its volcanic black sand seabed. This creates a unique muck-diving environment. You can see rare creatures like Hippocampus bargibanti seahorses and ornate ghost pipefish. The area also has coral-covered walls and the Japanese Wreck, offering a diverse underwater world.

mainEntity.name: Are Amed’s dive sites suitable for beginners or families?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Amed is great for beginners and families. Places like Jemeluk have easy shore entries. This makes it safe and fun for all.

mainEntity.name: How does seasonal weather affect diving conditions in Amed?

acceptedAnswer.text: The water in Amed stays warm all year, between 27-30°C. In the dry season (April-October), you might need a 3mm wetsuit. But in winter, a 5mm wetsuit is better. Visibility is always good, at 15m+, and summer is calmer.

mainEntity.name: What marine life specialties can macro photographers find in Amed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Macro photographers will love Amed’s night dives. You can see creatures like harlequin shrimp. Bunutan’s muck sites are home to mimic octopuses. The area’s rich biodiversity, thanks to the Coral Triangle, offers a chance to see pygmy seahorses on Jemeluk Wall’s sea fans.

mainEntity.name: How does Amed compare to neighboring Tulamben for dive experiences?

acceptedAnswer.text: Amed and Tulamben both have volcanic origins, but Amed offers more variety. Jemeluk Wall’s 40m drop-offs are different from Tulamben’s USS Liberty wreck. Amed’s sites are spread out, reducing crowds. It has walls, wrecks, and black sand slopes for all interests.

mainEntity.name: What safety infrastructure supports diving in Amed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Amed has a hyperbaric chamber in Denpasar, 3 hours away. Reputable operators like Dune Atlantis International follow strict safety rules. Sites like Pyramids have easy slopes for safe ascents. Shore entries also reduce risks from boats.

mainEntity.name: Can freedivers enjoy Amed’s underwater terrain?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, freedivers will love Amed. The clear water and shallow reefs are perfect. Bali Reef Divers offers guided freediving sessions. You can explore swim-throughs at Pyramids or vertical walls at Jemeluk.

mainEntity.name: What logistical considerations should divers plan for when visiting Amed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most dive centers, like Momo Dive Center, arrange airport transfers. The drive from Ngurah Rai is 3 hours. While “jukung” boats are available, most sites have shore entries. Staying at beachfront resorts helps you dive more, with breaks to watch traditional salt farming.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to visit Raja Ampat for diving?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best time to dive is from October to April. This season attracts mantas and has stable water temperatures. You’ll enjoy clear visibility and see mantas at Manta Ridge.

mainEntity.name: What makes Raja Ampat's marine life unique compared to other dive destinations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Raja Ampat is home to the richest marine life. You’ll see 10x more coral diversity than the Caribbean and triple the fish species of the Galapagos. Expect to see unique creatures like walking sharks and Misool’s stingless jellyfish.

mainEntity.name: Are there budget-friendly diving options in Raja Ampat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! There are affordable options. Partner resorts offer access to house reefs like Sorido Bay. Papua Diving provides all-inclusive rates and photography workshops.

mainEntity.name: What skills do I need for Raja Ampat's dive conditions?

acceptedAnswer.text: You’ll need skills for moderate currents. Sites like Cape Kri require SMB skills. Dives range from 18-30m, with opportunities to see a lot of marine life.

mainEntity.name: Can I see manta rays while diving in Raja Ampat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. Manta Ridge is known for guaranteed manta sightings. Papua Diving offers special dawn dives to see mantas and schooling fusiliers.

mainEntity.name: What underwater photography opportunities exist?

acceptedAnswer.text: SEACAM lighting rigs are perfect for capturing underwater scenes. You can photograph blue-ringed octopuses and flamboyant cuttlefish. The P47 plane wreck offers great wide-angle shots.

mainEntity.name: How does Raja Ampat's biodiversity compare to other regions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Raja Ampat has 1,606 fish species and 553 corals. You’ll see 75% of the world’s coral species here. The “Aquarium” near Kri Island is incredibly diverse.

mainEntity.name: Are there wreck diving opportunities in Raja Ampat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! The P47 Plane Wreck is a must-see. It’s home to lionfish schools and offers great photo opportunities. Papua Diving guides will help you get the best shots.

mainEntity.name: What makes Citrus Ridge a must-dive site?

acceptedAnswer.text: Citrus Ridge offers a unique dive experience. You’ll see orange soft corals and purple anthias clouds. It’s a great place to see rare species like the Raja Ampat goby.

mainEntity.name: Do liveaboard options exist for exploring remote sites?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Papua Diving offers liveaboards to remote sites. You can dive the B-24 bomber wreck and see Blue Magic’s spawning aggregations. Their boats have photography workstations for reviewing your photos.

mainEntity.name: Where is Mocean Beach Resort?

acceptedAnswer.text: On Pantai Moro (Moro Beach) in West Sumbawa, Indonesia. It’s about 30 minutes by car from Poto Tano ferry port and around 2 hours 15 minutes from Sumbawa Besar airport (SWQ). We arrange pickups from both.

mainEntity.name: Is Mocean a dive resort or a surf resort?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. We run a full dive center with a custom-built boat, gear lockers, a camera room, a training pool and PADI courses. Northern Rights breaks right in front of the resort, with Middle Reef and Dirty Hippies a short walk down the beach.

mainEntity.name: How much does a room cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard Rooms are IDR 1,690,000 to 2,100,000 a night and Deluxe Garden View Bungalows are IDR 2,200,000 to 2,750,000, depending on season. Rates cover two guests, breakfast, tax and service. Stays of three nights or more booked direct get a discount.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to visit West Sumbawa?

acceptedAnswer.text: May to October is dry season, with the most consistent surf and the clearest water. Our dive season runs 1 April to 31 October. November to April is greener and quieter, with lower room rates.

mainEntity.name: Can I visit for the day without staying?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Day guests are welcome to dive with us, and a pool day pass costs IDR 300,000 (10:00 to 17:00), with IDR 200,000 of that usable in the restaurant.

mainEntity.name: How do I book?

acceptedAnswer.text: Message us on WhatsApp at +62 821 4419 1647 or email bookings@moceanbeachresort.com with your dates. Booking direct gets you the multi-night discount and help with transfers.

itemListElement.name: How to Get to Sumbawa from Bali and Lombok

mainEntity.name: What is the easiest way to get to Sumbawa?

acceptedAnswer.text: The quickest and simplest route is a direct flight from Bali to Sumbawa Besar (SWQ), you can arrive on the same day with minimal fuss. Alternatively, flying to Lombok and taking the ferry to Poto Tano is a popular and scenic choice. Either way, we can arrange your transfers end to end.

mainEntity.name: Is there a direct ferry from Bali to Sumbawa?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, there's no single ferry that goes straight from Bali to Sumbawa. You'll cross in two stages: first from Bali (Padang Bai) to Lombok (Lembar), then across Lombok to Kayangan for the ferry to Poto Tano in West Sumbawa. Flying to Lombok first lets you skip the long first ferry leg.

mainEntity.name: Which airport should I choose when visiting West Sumbawa?

acceptedAnswer.text: For West Sumbawa, choose Sumbawa Besar (SWQ), it's the closest airport to our coast and the Poto Tano ferry port. Bima (BMU) on the east side is better suited to travellers heading to Lakey Peak or Mount Tambora. If you're staying with us, SWQ or a flight into Lombok (LOP) followed by the ferry are your best bets.

mainEntity.name: Can my accommodation help arrange transportation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes and we'd be delighted to. We regularly organise airport transfers, ferry connections, private boats, and helicopter flights for our guests. Just let us know your arrival details and we'll handle the rest, so your journey to Sumbawa is as smooth and stress-free as possible.

mainEntity.name: How difficult is the trek to Kalela Waterfall?

acceptedAnswer.text: It’s an easy-to-moderate walk suitable for most reasonably active visitors. From the parking area, you’ll trek around 30 to 45 minutes along a rocky path through farmland and forest. It’s not strenuous, but sturdy shoes with good grip make a real difference, especially if the ground is damp.

mainEntity.name: What is the best time to visit Kalela Waterfall?

acceptedAnswer.text: The rainy season (roughly November to April) brings the fullest, most impressive flow, while the dry months can leave the falls gentler. Whatever the season, aim for mid-morning to early afternoon — that’s when the sun filters through the trees and lights up the tosca pool most beautifully.

mainEntity.name: Can I swim in the pond at Kalela Waterfall?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! The natural pool below the falls is calm, shallow, and refreshingly cool, making it lovely for a dip. The gentle water flow even lets you stand beneath the cascade like a natural shower. Bring water shoes if you have them, and always take care on the slippery rocks.

mainEntity.name: Is Kalela Waterfall suitable for children and families?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be a wonderful family outing, as long as little ones are comfortable with a short walk and you keep a close eye on them around the water and rocks. Because facilities are basic, pack water, snacks, and spare dry clothes to keep everyone happy.

mainEntity.name: How far is Kalela Waterfall from Sumbawa Besar?

acceptedAnswer.text: Kalela is roughly 130 kilometres from Sumbawa Besar, which works out to about a three-hour drive. If you’re staying on the west coast near Taliwang or the Poto Tano area, you’ll be far closer, often within an hour of the trailhead.

mainEntity.name: What is a ninja manta?

acceptedAnswer.text: A ninja manta is a manta ray with an all-black or almost all-black body. Polong, a regular at Ju-Ju’s Jackpot, is black on top with a striking white mark on his belly.

mainEntity.name: Where is Ju-Ju's Jackpot?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ju-Ju’s Jackpot is one of our West Sumbawa dive sites, named after Julie, our first instructor. Manta rays chain-feed there in plankton-rich water.

mainEntity.name: How do I dive with the mantas?

acceptedAnswer.text: Join one of our guided boat dives (two-tank boat dives are IDR 2,200,000) and tell us you’d like to visit Ju-Ju’s Jackpot. Mantas are wild animals, so sightings depend on conditions and no dive is guaranteed.

mainEntity.name: What is the best tide for Scar Reef?

acceptedAnswer.text: High tide works best. It brings fuller waves and more water over the sharp coral. At low tide the reef is exposed and the barrels close out more often.

mainEntity.name: When is the best season to surf Scar Reef?

acceptedAnswer.text: The dry season, roughly April to October, when consistent Indian Ocean swells reach West Sumbawa. Early in the season the winds are often lighter.

mainEntity.name: How far is Scar Reef from Mocean Beach Resort?

acceptedAnswer.text: About an hour’s drive. Northern Rights, Middle Reef and Dirty Hippies are much closer to the resort for the smaller days.

description: Agal Waterfall is a full-day jungle trek in West Sumbawa with river crossings and clear pools to swim in. See what the hike involves, then book your guide.
og:title: Agal Waterfall Sumbawa | Trek Guide & Guided Day Trip
og:description: Agal Waterfall is a full-day jungle trek in West Sumbawa with river crossings and clear pools to swim in. See what the hike involves, then book your guide.

@graph.name: Agal Waterfall Sumbawa | Trek Guide & Guided Day Trip
@graph.description: Agal Waterfall is a full-day jungle trek in West Sumbawa with river crossings and clear pools to swim in. See what the hike involves, then book your guide.

mainEntity.name: How long is the hike to Agal Waterfall?

acceptedAnswer.text: About two hours along a jungle trail with several river crossings. With the drive and a meal afterwards, plan for a full day.

mainEntity.name: Is the Agal Waterfall trek difficult?

acceptedAnswer.text: It’s challenging rather than technical. Expect rocky paths, steady climbs and wading through streams. Reasonably fit walkers manage it fine with good shoes.

mainEntity.name: Can you swim at Agal Waterfall?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The falls drop into clear pools that are good for a swim after the hike.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a guide for Agal Waterfall?

acceptedAnswer.text: We recommend one. The trail crosses rivers and isn’t signposted, and a local guide knows where to cross safely when water levels change.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to visit Agal Waterfall?

acceptedAnswer.text: The flow is strongest during and just after the rainy season (November to April). The dry season (May to October) makes the trail and river crossings easier.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to hire a surf guide in Sumbawa?

acceptedAnswer.text: It’s highly recommended, especially for your first visit or for the heavier reef breaks. A good guide reads the tides and swell, knows which spot suits the day’s conditions, and keeps you safe over shallow coral. Even confident surfers save time and score better waves with local knowledge on their side.

mainEntity.name: Are there surfboard rentals available in Sumbawa?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many surf resorts, camps, and beachside shops rent boards, and some offer lessons for beginners. That said, Sumbawa is remote and selection can be limited, so if you ride a specific board or need a gun for bigger days, it’s smart to bring your own — plus backup fins, leashes, and wax.

mainEntity.name: How many days should I spend surfing in Sumbawa?

acceptedAnswer.text: We’d suggest at least five to seven days to account for travel time and to give yourself a good window of swell and tides. A week lets you settle into the rhythm, explore multiple breaks, and enjoy a rest day or two without feeling rushed. Longer is even better if your schedule allows.

mainEntity.name: What should I pack for a surfing trip to Sumbawa?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bring your boards and plenty of spares (leashes, fins, wax), reef booties for shallow sessions, a rash guard, and reef-safe sunscreen. Add a basic first-aid kit for coral scrapes, a dry bag, and light, quick-drying clothing. Since supplies are limited on the island, it pays to arrive well prepared.

mainEntity.name: Are there accommodations near Sumbawa's surf spots?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. From simple surf camps and homestays to comfortable beachfront resorts, both coasts have places to stay close to the waves. On the west coast, being based near the Kertasari and Moro Bay breaks means you can check the surf before breakfast — which is exactly what makes staying with us so convenient.

mainEntity.name: Is the Sumbawa surf camp good for beginners?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Beginners learn at Middle Reef, which has softer take-offs and mellow shoulders. Private lessons with a local coach cost IDR 1,000,000 per person, for up to two people.

mainEntity.name: When is the best season to surf West Sumbawa?

acceptedAnswer.text: April to October is the most consistent, with dry-season swell and offshore winds in the mornings. Waves still break the rest of the year, with fewer people in the water.

mainEntity.name: Which surf breaks can I walk to from Mocean?

acceptedAnswer.text: Northern Rights is right in front of the resort, Middle Reef is next to it, and Dirty Hippies is about a 15-minute walk down the beach.

mainEntity.name: Can I rent a surfboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, boards are IDR 150,000 a day. Tell us your height, weight and level before you arrive and we’ll set one aside.

mainEntity.name: How is this different from a Bali surf camp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Smaller crowds. West Sumbawa has a handful of resorts along the coast, so you share Northern Rights with a few people instead of a full line-up.

mainEntity.name: Is Sumbawa worth visiting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if you like surf, reefs and quiet roads. Sumbawa is bigger than Bali and far less developed, so you get uncrowded waves, empty beaches and waterfalls without the crowds.

mainEntity.name: What is the best time to visit Sumbawa?

acceptedAnswer.text: May to October is dry season, with sunny days, steady surf and clear water. November to April brings rain, greener hills and fuller waterfalls.

mainEntity.name: How do I get to Sumbawa from Bali?

acceptedAnswer.text: The quickest way is a direct flight from Bali to Sumbawa Besar (SWQ). You can also fly to Lombok and take the hourly ferry from Kayangan to Poto Tano.

mainEntity.name: Where should I stay in West Sumbawa?

acceptedAnswer.text: Stay on the coast near the surf and reefs. Mocean Beach Resort on Pantai Moro has three surf breaks within walking distance, a dive center and a beachfront restaurant.

mainEntity.name: Is Mocean Beach Resort right on the beach?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The pool, restaurant, lounge and yoga chalet sit on the shoreline of Pantai Moro. The rooms face tropical gardens a few steps back from the sand.

mainEntity.name: Do the rooms have sea views?

acceptedAnswer.text: The rooms look onto the gardens. For sea views, the pool deck and Mutiara restaurant face the ocean directly.

mainEntity.name: Is the resort good for families?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Rooms take up to three guests and a cot or child’s fold-out bed can be added. The house reef has shallow snorkeling and the pool is right by the beach.
